items.title: John Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001
items.q: I went back to the Schillinger House and asked for my application fee back.

ctx.x: Yeah. We’re taking a little break there, yeah. Yeah, “you’ll be back.” I said, “okay,” so I hopped on and went to Boston. Because I knew I had met somebody that was originally from Vero Beach by the name of Henderson and he says, “well come on up we’ll help you out.” So I went up there and I found out he was a Pullman porter. So they put me up in the Pullman porter’s place for, what, seven dollars a week. So he gave me a room and I tried to wait tables. I remember the first job I ever tried to do up there and the…

on? That’s not a tux. Out.” So I was out. So anyway I ended up getting a job at Steuben’s Restaurant in Boston as a dishwasher. And I washed a few pots and pans. And I think that lasted a little over a week too. But in the meantime I went back to the Schillinger House and asked for my application fee back. I think it was like $25 or something.
